subject.title: feat(code-mode): Swarms — agent fan-out and orchestration in code mode

question: Should OpenClaw make a deliberate exception to its current guardrail and adopt a core code-mode Swarm orchestration framework, or keep multi-agent orchestration at the existing session-tool boundary?
rationale: The requested work is a new core framework with public tool/configuration, lifecycle, approval, and UI implications, and `VISION.md` expressly defers this class of heavy orchestration by default.

options.title: Keep the current boundary
options.body: Decline the full core Swarm framework for now and continue improving the existing bounded session-tool primitives when concrete reliability gaps arise.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow design phase
options.body: Authorize a maintainer-owned design that proves one missing primitive and its safety/compatibility contract before proposing runtime or UI work.

options.title: Adopt the full Swarm program
options.body: Explicitly accept the roadmap exception and assign owners for the core runtime, code-mode, protocol, persistence, UI, and channel delivery contracts.

recommendation.title: Keep the current boundary
recommendation.body: Decline the full core Swarm framework for now and continue improving the existing bounded session-tool primitives when concrete reliability gaps arise.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history and the issue itself connect steipete most directly to the subagent orchestration and session-tool boundary.
